chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Yazid, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani, said:
I wrote to him: Fur and hair from that whose flesh is not eaten falls onto my garment, without taqiyyah and without necessity. So he wrote, peace be upon him: Salat is not permissible in it.

key_terms.الْوَبَرُ: fur or fine animal hair that falls onto a garment
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: dissimulation for protection under threat or harm
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: a state of necessity or compulsion
key_terms.لَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: an animal whose flesh is not lawful to eat

ai.seo_question: Is salat valid in clothing contaminated with fur or hair from animals whose flesh is not eaten?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat in a garment upon which fur or hair from an animal whose flesh is not lawful to eat has fallen. The Imam عليه السلام replies that salat in such a garment is not permissible when there is neither taqiyyah nor necessity.
